title: When a node re-runs: fingerprints, the NaN trick, not_idempotent

questions.q: IS_CHANGED returns True on every call. What happens on the second queue, with nothing else changed?
options: The node comes from the cache
questions.answer: The node comes from the cache
questions.why: It's a value in the key, not an answer. The same value gives the same key.

questions.q: Which of these makes a node run on every queue?
questions.why: A new NaN never equals the stored one. math.nan is one shared object, and a real run showed 1 execution in 3 queues.

questions.q: What does a fingerprint see for an input fed by a wire?
options: It is not called at all
questions.why: IsChangedCache calls get_input_data with no execution list, so linked values are marked missing.

questions.q: Two identical copies of a not_idempotent node sit in a graph. You queue twice, unchanged. How many executions in total?
questions.why: The id joins the key, so each copy has its own result. On the second queue both are cached.

questions.q: An input has max=10, and your validate_inputs takes that input as an argument. A value of 100 arrives. What does the engine do?
options: Passes it to your function and skips its own range check
questions.answer: Passes it to your function and skips its own range check
questions.why: The range check runs only for inputs not named in the validator. So your validator must check it.

questions.q: Your validate_inputs ends with no return statement. What happens?
questions.why: Anything except True counts as failure, and that includes None.
